quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye and Richard Jefferson discuss the origin of Taco Tuesday
quotes.excerpt: You didn't even start that. I did. Remember we were on the airplane?

text_blocks.speaker: Richard Jefferson
text_blocks.text: Do you remember when LeBron started the Taco Tuesday?

text_blocks.speaker: Channing Frye
text_blocks.text: You didn't even start that. I did. Remember we were on the airplane? I would always say if they have options, do you want a burrito, this or this? I would always get the burrito. He goes, Channing is always over there eating burritos and I go, I know because it is Taco Tuesday.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye and Richard Jefferson discuss the 2016 Cavaliers team chemistry
quotes.excerpt: Everyone gives you credit for being the final piece of the puzzle, not only on the court.

text_blocks.speaker: Richard Jefferson
text_blocks.text: Everyone gives you credit for being the final piece of the puzzle, not only on the court, but also in the locker room. What did you notice in the locker room when you first showed up?

text_blocks.speaker: Channing Frye
text_blocks.text: You were very unappreciative of what you had. I was three and a half hours Scott Skiles practices to go into a game to go, well, come on, get the belt. It was like, you know, I had seen you two weeks before that. We had practiced so hard to try to beat you and you were like, oh, we are just going to beat you by 20. And like you just walked on the court and beat us. And so when I was out, I was like, man, you don't practice that hard. You have LeBron, Kyrie and Kevin and you don't even talk.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye on the tactical challenges of playing four-on-four in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: The fact that you are playing four-on-four. I think a coach told me Isaiah Thomas, Zeke told me.

text_blocks.speaker: Richard Jefferson
text_blocks.text: Which part of your game still gets talked about too simply?

text_blocks.speaker: Channing Frye
text_blocks.text: The fact that you are playing four-on-four. I think a coach told me Isaiah Thomas, Zeke told me, I will pay somebody twice what they are worth if I can like put this, he was talking about J.J. Redick. He is like his value comes from you are playing four-on-four in an NBA court because you cannot leave him, you like have to touch him. We used to call it Frye Island. Right, Frye Island. You could watch the Toronto series and Bismack Biyombo was looking at me and I was like, you are either going to try and block that or I am going to shoot this. So come on, let's just hold hands. I am not going to shoot, but this is my job for you to stand right next to me.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye and Richard Jefferson on the 2016 NBA Finals loss
quotes.excerpt: That might have been the greatest depression that I think I have felt in a non-elimination game.

text_blocks.speaker: Richard Jefferson
text_blocks.text: Take us through that moment where Game 4, we lose at home. That might have been the greatest depression that I think I have felt in a non-elimination game.

text_blocks.speaker: Channing Frye
text_blocks.text: So my family always comes to the games and after this game, my wife, my kids are a little at the time and Lauren looks at me and goes, oh, we are going to let Daddy go home by himself. I am never going to forget her face looking at me and going, oh, and like shoes, our children away. Like Channing is going to either lose it and cry, like, but James Jones and the other guys brainwashed each other, we brainwashed each other into thinking it is not them, it is us.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye on how adversity shaped his perspective as a teammate
quotes.excerpt: I think it made me a better teammate because it put again things in perspective of like.

text_blocks.speaker: Richard Jefferson
text_blocks.text: Did going through that make you a better teammate, because you knew basketball could get taken away without asking permission?

text_blocks.speaker: Channing Frye
text_blocks.text: I think it made me a better teammate because it put again things in perspective of like, do I really even want to do this? There were certain days that I would cry going to the gym and then have that hour or two hours or three hours, whatever it was, that like I didn't think about that. And so I think for me, I appreciated basketball differently and so I am more intense now or after that about taking advantage of your opportunity while you have it because you never know what is going to happen.
